result.rationale: The diff confirms the inconsistency: in BiginCalendarService, refreshOAuthTokens is called with `"zoho-bigin", credentialId` while every sibling call site (google-calendar, hubspot, lark, office365, msteams, webex, zohocrm, zoomvideo) passes `credential.userId`. The sync path posts this value as `calcomUserId` to the parent app, so a credential id is sent where a user id is expected. The exact semantics of `credentialId` aren't visible in the diff, but the mechanism is verifiable and clearly a defect if it is not a user id.

judged_text: Bigin passes credentialId as refreshOAuthTokens' userId argument — every sibling call site passes credential.userId — so the sync request posts the credential's own DB id as calcomUserId. In sync mode the parent app receives a credential id where the protocol's calcomUserId is expected, resolves no user (or the wrong one), and its returned tokens are persisted under this credential — Bigin credential sync never works and can silently attach the wrong entity's tokens.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call is `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. The helper `refreshOAuthTokens` treats its 3rd argument as `userId` and, in sync mode, posts it as `calcomUserId` (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()`). Every other updated call site in the diff passes `credential.userId`, so passing `credentialId` here will send the credential record id instead of the Cal.com user id, breaking credential sync for Bigin (or mapping tokens to the wrong user) when `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is enabled.
